blocks.text: Programs often need to choose what to do depending on conditions, or to repeat actions many times. Control structures do this, and there are two main kinds: decision making and looping.

blocks.alt: Left: a flowchart testing whether the weather is sunny, then rainy, leading to wear sunglasses, take an umbrella or enjoy your day, with notes on if, if-else, short-hand if-else, if-elif-else and nesting. Right: a flowchart that sets number to 1 and, while number is less than 10, prints it and adds 1, with notes on while, for and range().
blocks.caption: Decision making and loops (original diagram after topic 2.4).
blocks.long_description: An if-elif-else chain tests conditions in order and runs the block of the first true one: if the weather is sunny the program says wear sunglasses, otherwise if it is rainy it says take an umbrella, otherwise enjoy your day. A while loop checks its condition before every pass: starting with number equal to 1, while number is less than 10 it prints the number and adds 1, so it prints 1 to 9 and stops when the condition becomes false. A for loop takes each item of a sequence in turn, and range() produces sequences of numbers such as 0 to 4.

blocks.prompt: Name the two main kinds of control structure.
blocks.explanation: Decision making (if, if-else, if-elif-else) and looping (while and for loops).

items: Control structures: decision making (choose an action by a condition) and looping (repeat an action).
